stage_01_record.assay_method: postoperative clinical examination including SD-OCT, fundus photography, fluorescein angiography
stage_01_record.experimental_conditions: 71-year-old male patient on systemic amiodarone (dose and duration not specified) undergoing vitrectomy for epiretinal membrane; operative time and illumination within normal range.
stage_01_record.extra_details: Single case report; no rechallenge. Authors hypothesize amiodarone predisposed to phototoxicity.
stage_01_record.light_conditions: operating microscope light during surgery (wavelength and dose not specified)
stage_01_record.measurement_text: retinal phototoxicity: pigment clumping, fibrosis, intraretinal cystic changes, loss of ellipsoid layer, subretinal fibrosis, hyperpigmentation on fundus photography and fluorescein angiogram
stage_01_record.qualifying_conditions: mechanical disruption of retina from ERM may have contributed
stage_01_record.support_text: We hypothesize that our patient's postoperative findings are consistent with phototoxicity as a result of photosensitisizing effects of amiodarone. ... Therefore, given that amiodarone deposits are found in retinal pigment epithelial cells and ganglion cells, and that amiodarone has photosensitizing properties on the skin and in RPE cells in vitro, there is a theoretical risk of retinal phototoxicity. Our patient's post-operative exam and imaging findings are consistent with retinal phototoxicity. ... We presume that the use of systemic amiodarone may have predisposed our patient to retinal phototoxicity.
